SAN FRANCISCO — A Florida man who sought health guidance on ChatGPT sued OpenAI Wednesday, claiming the artificial intelligence chatbot gave him dangerously inaccurate medical advice that led him to delay seeking professional treatment for a pulmonary embolism. items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary: OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. items.title: Google promised Gemini 3.5 Pro in June.
items.summary:
Google promised Gemini 3.5 Pro in June.

June passed. July came and is going already. 

As of July 21 Google’s public position is that Gemini 3.5 Pro is “currently testing with partners” with no confirmed release date.

Bloomberg and other outlets have reported that Gemini 3.5 Pro is behind schedule, with Google pushing back its launch window, though Google has not publicly blamed specific coding performance failures.

Meanwhile Google shipped Gemini 3.6 Flash on July 21, along with 3.5 Flash-Lite and a restricted cybersecurity model called 3.5 Flash Cyber. Faster and cheaper, but still not the flagship Pro model developers have been waiting on since May.

The current live Pro model in Google’s lineup remains Gemini 3.1 Pro.

If you have been holding off on building something while waiting for 3.5 Pro, stop waiting. There is no confirmed date. Build with what is available today.

items.title: A lot of people have been dunking on gemini 3.6 flash since it dropped.
items.summary:
A lot of people have been dunking on gemini 3.6 flash since it dropped.

The claim: it didn’t get smarter on any level.

That part’s actually true, considering it scores a 50 on the intelligence index, exact same as 3.5 flash, with no iq gain.

But as someone who runs automations on flash tier models, & also use it as a fallback on Hermes; intelligence was never the thing holding those back.

What actually matters when a model’s running a task 200 times an hour is speed, cost per run, & whether it reliably calls the right tool.

& that’s exactly what they’ve moved:

➥ osworld-verified jumped to 83% from 78.4.

➥ output tokens dropped hard on deepswe, with fewer loops.

➥ cheaper per task, & not just per token.

So is it a smarter model? 
Maybe not.

Plus they’ve also fallen behind on the top 5 labs.

But it’s a cheaper, faster, more reliable worker for agents, and maybe that’s the upgrade that actually counts, & not another point on a benchmark chart.

Not saying the crowd is wrong to care about that.

Just the wrong lens for what this release might’ve actually been built for.

That said.

The flash drops are clearly filler while gemini 3.5 pro sits stuck in training.

But they’ve also announced pretraining for gemini 4 & they’re calling it their most ambitious run yet.

So just maybe they’re not completely cooked yet.

Curious to know what everyone else is running their flash tier models for.

items.summary: # The AI Tool Changing How Doctors Practice Medicine. Most physicians now utilize AI, like OpenEvidence, for clinical decision-making, streamlining access to drug guidelines and research, which saves time and improves patient care. OpenEvidence, a $12 billion company used by over 65% of U.S. doctors, offers concise, evidence-based summaries, enhancing efficiency and knowledge across specialties. Whether patients are aware of it or not, most physicians now use AI to guide their decision-making. Doctors are using conversational AI models to quickly answer clinical questions, clarify drug dosing guidelines, investigate drug interactions, and stay up to date with the latest research studies. According to the company, its software, which allows doctors to ask complex, highly specific clinical questions in plain English, is used by more than 65% of the physicians in the U.S. Backed by venture heavyweights like Sequoia and Google Ventures, and boasting partnerships with reputable organizations such as *The New England Journal of Medicine,* the company is now valued at $12 billion.

items.summary: # NIH joins Trump’s $5B AI mission with biomedical research push. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services announced new efforts Wednesday aligned with President Donald Trump’s artificial intelligence-driven Genesis Mission. HHS plans to support biomedical research and accelerate discoveries, with a particular focus on chronic disease, a key priority of Secretary Robert F. The commitments include efforts to uncover the root causes of chronic disease, unlock treatments for pediatric cancer and accelerate drug discovery and clinical translation. The efforts stem from the president’s November 2025 executive order launching the Genesis Mission, a coordinated national initiative aimed at using AI, advanced computing and federal research resources to accelerate scientific discovery. In collaboration with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, HHS will launch a series of “National Science and Technology Challenges” encouraging scientists to apply AI to pressing health problems, according to a July 22 statement.

items.title: Elon Musk's solar ambitions have shifted from powering homes to powering Tesla's AI era - Business Insider
items.summary: # Elon Musk's solar ambitions have shifted from powering homes to powering Tesla's AI era. About a decade ago, Tesla entered its solar-for-homes era with its contentious acquisition of SolarCity. Now, Tesla's solar dreams are taking a different shape as the company enters its AI era. ContourGlobal, a global power producer, announced on Tuesday that Tesla signed a long-term agreement to purchase 1 terawatt-hour of electricity a year from Project Sterling, ContourGlobal's solar and battery storage project in Arizona. The deals reflect Elon Musk's latest arc from leveraging solar power for consumer homes to solar use in industrial settings, which could include AI infrastructure. In recent years, however, Musk has increasingly focused his solar ambitions on the grid, as AI is expected to drive surging power demand and Tesla stakes more of its future on AI and robotics. In a January earnings call, the CEO said "the solar opportunity is underestimated," and that solar paired with batteries was the "best way" to add more power to the grid.

items.summary: # Tesla's 2026.26 Summer Update: Photos & Videos. Packed with new features, quality-of-life improvements, and cabin entertainment additions, the release brings a long list of updates to the fleet. The Summer 2026 Software Update began rolling out publicly over the weekend as software update 2026.26, following Tesla’s original announcement last week. Here’s a breakdown of some of the biggest additions in this feature drop:. As detailed in our breakdown of Tesla’s new Grok integration for vehicle functions, owners can place phone calls, search for and play music, adjust cabin climate, open the glovebox, and adjust driving settings like Steering Weight simply by talking naturally. As shown in our hands-on video with Tesla’s redesigned Caraoke app with live scoring, the new layout swaps static text for pitch lines and note-timing bars. Vehicle customization is expanding beyond the cabin touchscreen with software update 2026.26 and Tesla mobile app version 4.59.0. With the Summer Update, Tesla is adding the ability to lock touch controls on the rear display.

items.title: NHTSA Rejects Petition Seeking Tesla Door-Release Defect Probe - Insurance Journal
items.summary: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has denied a petition seeking a defect investigation into the emergency mechanical door release on about 180,000 Tesla Model 3 vehicles. NHTSA said the petition did not present evidence of a likely safety-related defect warranting an investigation and that the issue would be more appropriately addressed through an ongoing rulemaking process. The petition covered about 180,000 model-year 2022 Tesla Model 3 vehicles and alleged the manual door release was difficult to locate after a crash if the vehicle lost power, increasing the risk of occupants getting trapped. The agency said it had granted a separate petition to consider whether to issue regulations to require an emergency door egress system to address the risk of occupant entrapment in vehicles during electrical power failures. The agency said it had a single consumer complaint involving a 2022 Model 3 that alleged the mechanical door release was concealed and unlabeled after the vehicle lost electrical power in a front-impact crash.

items.title: Tesla's 2026.26 Summer Update Lets You Video Conference on Google Meet, Teams & Discord - Not a Tesla App
items.summary: Rather than developing separate apps for the many communications platforms people use these days, Tesla is granting its in-car web browser access to the cabin camera as well as the interior microphone. This opens the door to using any video conferencing app that has a web interface. While the Summer Update delivers highlight features like a redesigned Caraoke app with live scoring, new Grok voice commands for vehicle functions like climate, and fresh welcome animations for newer Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, browser-based webcam access finally delivers on Musk’s longstanding promise of video conferencing capabilities in Tesla vehicles. By giving the native browser access to the interior cabin camera and microphone, owners can join video calls across any browser-supported platform, including Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, X Spaces, and Discord. Since Tesla is already cropping the cabin camera video feed to focus in on the driver, face tracking would make for an excellent quality-of-life addition down the line.
